clue.text: Take place of one imprisoned for begging

indicators.note: the Roman one is locked up inside the longer verb, as a prisoner sits within walls

parts.note: to supplant someone is to take their place
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone stands in for a prisoner who has been jailed for begging in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A suppliant person asks humbly and earnestly, which is to say begging for something.

clue.text: Be off road at first, taken in by fraud

indicators.note: being taken in by something means being held inside it, here inside the swindle

parts.note: a scam is a fraud or swindle

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word road is wanted

explanation.surface: A motorist heads off down the road, having been duped by a con from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Scram is a brusque imperative telling someone to go away, the same as be off.

clue.text: Settle up for early music, getting satisfaction at last?

parts.note: to pay off a debt is to settle up
old scores are written music from long ago

explanation.surface: Someone settles a bill for a concert of early music and finally feels satisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads the whole phrase in its idiomatic sense of taking long-awaited revenge; the question mark flags that the wordplay pieces are taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay off old scores is the idiom for avenging old grievances, finally obtaining satisfaction.

clue.text: Stick with this, being a sucker

definitions.text: Stick with this, being a sucker

parts.words: Stick with this, being a sucker
parts.note: a sweet on a stick that one sucks; sucker is also the American word for such a sweet, while the surface reads as advice to a gullible person

explanation.surface: Advice to persevere with something, even if it makes you look gullible.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard sweet mounted on a stick, called a sucker in America, is exactly what is described.

clue.text: Unusual article found in abandoned clay-pit

indicators.note: the article is discovered sitting inside the rearranged letters
abandoned suggests something let loose and disorderly, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An unusual object turns up in a disused clay pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' rearranges CLAYPIT into TYPICL, and 'found in' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Atypical means not typical, that is unusual or out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Roof covering of church indicated

parts.note: that is the word used to point something out, so it stands for indicated

explanation.surface: Someone points out the roof covering on a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatch is straw or reed laid as a roof covering on cottages.

clue.text: Exclamation of delight about politician's

annotationWithheld.why: 'Exclamation of delight about politician's (5)' as held: OOH round MP gives the letters, but no word defines OOMPH; the definition (probably a word for vigour after politician's) appears lost in OCR and no search found the full clue

clue.text: He asked for more from old organ

parts.note: the liver is a bodily organ

explanation.surface: Someone requests more of something taken from an old organ.
explanation.walkthrough: In Dickens's Oliver Twist the workhouse boy famously asks for more gruel.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Twist is the Dickens orphan who notoriously asked the workhouse master for more.

clue.text: When presents are given to women a ruined by gin?

definitions.text: When presents are given to women a ruined by gin?

parts.words: When presents are given to women a ruined by gin?
parts.note: gin is nicknamed mother's ruin, so women ruined by gin are mothers, and the day they receive presents is the British spring holiday in their honour

explanation.surface: A question about when gifts go to women who have been brought low by drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray 'a' looks like an OCR blemish; the clue works as a whole. Gin's old British nickname is 'mother's ruin'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the British Lent Sunday on which children give gifts and cards to their mums.

clue.text: Earth-shattering material of unfeigned sincerity

indicators.note: something shattered is broken into pieces, so the letters of the word are scrambled

parts.note: felt is a fabric or material made of matted fibres

explanation.surface: Some earth-shattering cloth is described as utterly sincere.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartfelt means deeply and sincerely felt, without any pretence.

clue.text: Prince, possibly, demanding initial change in allegiance

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for allegiance is swapped for another

parts.note: loyalty is allegiance to a cause or ruler

explanation.surface: A prince demands that his subjects transfer their loyalty.
explanation.walkthrough: Changing the L of LOYALTY to R gives the word; 'possibly' marks the prince as one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A prince is a member of the royal family, so is an example of royalty.

clue.text: A woman takes in extremely elegant song

indicators.note: the woman's name absorbs the other letters inside itself

parts.note: Rita is a woman's name

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so the first and last letters of elegant

explanation.surface: A woman absorbs a particularly graceful song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of 'elegant'; 'takes in' has the woman swallow them after her first letter, not at her edges.
explanation.definitionFit: An arietta is a short aria, a brief song in an opera or similar work.

clue.text: Greek character with note on fine clothing

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written on another comes after it

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A Greek figure, with a note attached, comments on fine clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: MUFTI is a British word for ordinary clothes worn by someone who usually wears uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Mufti means civilian dress worn by someone, such as a soldier, normally in uniform.

clue.text: Rise in books covering key part of army

indicators.note: the outer pieces cover the inner ones on either side

parts.note: taken as written
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books
C is a musical key
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: An army unit sees a rise in the number of books it holds.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is the British Army's Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers. 'covering' here has the two short words flank the key and corps, one each side.
explanation.definitionFit: An increment is an increase or rise, as in a step up a salary scale.

clue.text: Plan is pertinent, rubbing out a gangster

indicators.note: rubbing out removes something, here the letter a from the start of the word

parts.note: apropos means relevant or pertinent
taken as written
Al Capone is the archetypal gangster

explanation.surface: A scheme is deemed relevant because it involves bumping off a mobster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbing out' removes A from APROPOS, leaving PROPOS. It also puns on gangland slang for killing.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal is a plan or scheme put forward for consideration.

clue.text: Enjoyed being under a spell

definitions.meaning: having enjoyed something can mean having owned or held it, as in enjoyed great wealth
controlled by a demon or spirit, bewitched

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both owned or held and, separately, controlled by an evil spirit.

clue.text: It's all right to be nearly in line with wicket

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a fielding position close to the line of the stumps

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a fine fielding position is close to the line running through the wickets behind the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means satisfactory, and in cricket describes a position close to the line of the stumps.

clue.text: Appeal of former partner invited into functions with son

indicators.note: being invited into a place means going inside it

parts.note: sines are trigonometric functions
an ex is a former spouse or partner
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: An old flame is asked along to social functions with her son.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexiness is sexual attractiveness, that is allure or appeal.

clue.text: Entertainer put cape on person in box

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape
taken as written
a juror sits in the jury box in court

explanation.surface: A performer dons a cloak and climbs into a box, as in a magic trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put' just links the pieces. The 'box' is the jury box, not a magician's cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror is a magician who entertains audiences with tricks.

clue.text: Trouble over squadron leader's first drink

indicators.note: the leading letter of squadron is taken
over signals that the word for trouble is turned round

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A squadron leader's first drink causes some trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the word for trouble round, and the result follows the squadron leader's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda is a fizzy drink or soda water.

clue.text: Prayed, as Sir Percy Blakeney was said to?

definitions.text: as Sir Percy Blakeney was said to?
definitions.meaning: the Scarlet Pimpernel's rhyme says they seek him here and seek him there

explanation.walkthrough: Sir Percy Blakeney is the Scarlet Pimpernel: 'They seek him here, they seek him there.' Split, the answer gives BE SOUGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Besought is the past tense of beseech, meaning begged or prayed.

clue.text: Bernstein's book on spiny-finned fish

parts.note: Leonard Bernstein, the composer, was known as Lenny

explanation.surface: The composer Leonard Bernstein's book about a spiny fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Blennies are small spiny-finned fish of rock pools and coasts.

clue.text: Courses that may encourage one in middle age?

definitions.text: Courses that may encourage one in middle age?

parts.words: Courses that may encourage one in middle age?
parts.note: a lavish meal of many courses, which could bring on the thickening waistline of middle age known by the same word

explanation.surface: A question about classes that might motivate the middle-aged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courses' suggests education; here it means the courses of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A spread is a large meal, and middle-aged spread is weight gained around the waist.

clue.text: Oil sources requiring new clue? A pity

indicators.note: new means remade, so these letters are formed into something different

explanation.surface: A solver laments that a fresh clue is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the letters of CLUE and A PITY together.
explanation.definitionFit: Eucalyptus trees yield eucalyptus oil, so their plural form names the sources of that oil.

clue.text: Encounter love visiting fair

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone's home, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: just means fair or equitable
O is love, a score of nil in tennis

explanation.surface: Love comes into someone's life at a fair, leading to an encounter.
explanation.definitionFit: A joust is a combat between two knights, an encounter on horseback.

clue.text: Fearful old American abandoned Indonesian territory

indicators.note: abandoned means left behind, so these letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: timorous means nervous or fearful
US is short for the United States, hence American

explanation.surface: A nervous elderly American leaves a territory in Indonesia.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing O and US from the end of TIMOROUS leaves the island name.
explanation.definitionFit: Timor is an island in the Malay archipelago, whose western half belongs to Indonesia.

clue.text: It ensnares a dog endlessly

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the dog breed is dropped

parts.note: a springer is a spaniel breed

explanation.surface: A dog is endlessly getting itself caught in a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A springe is a noose or snare for catching small game, something that ensnares.

clue.text: Dignity a monk associated with Hines

parts.note: Earl Hines was a famous American jazz pianist, so Earl goes with Hines
Dom is a title given to Benedictine and other monks

explanation.surface: A monk with dignity is linked to someone named Hines.
explanation.walkthrough: Earl Hines was a celebrated jazz pianist. Dignity here means a rank or title, not poise.
explanation.definitionFit: Dignity can mean a high rank or title, and an earldom is the rank of an earl.

clue.text: Attractive female of the bashful kind

parts.note: Di is a woman's name, short for Diana
shy means bashful or timid

explanation.surface: A good-looking woman who is the bashful type.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishy is informal British slang for good-looking or sexually attractive.

clue.text: Apollyon's heavily armed warship

definitions.meaning: Apollyon, the angel of the abyss in Revelation, has a name meaning the one who ruins
a fast warship armed with guns and missiles

explanation.walkthrough: In Revelation 9:11, Apollyon is the Greek name for the angel of the bottomless pit; it means 'the one who destroys'.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollyon's name translates as the annihilator, and a fast escort warship bears the same title.
